name: Nullframe PalmSync Chrome-Interface Glove
description:
Precision-engineered to bridge organic hand and chrome forearm augmentation. Constructed from gunmetal-grey adaptive syn-neoprene with embedded conductive threading that maps to standard aug-port contact arrays. The glove terminates in a structured cuff with a magnetic locking ring that aligns flush against most mid-grade chrome forearm housings, creating a seamless visual and tactile join.

Finger segments are articulated with micro-flex panels allowing full dexterity. Available in full-finger and half-finger cuts. The dorsal surface features a subtle embossed circuit-trace pattern in matte black — functional, not decorative: it routes haptic return signals from the chrome to surviving nerve clusters.
functionality: Interfaces with standard aug-port arrays on chrome forearms. Haptic relay film transmits tactile feedback from prosthetic fingertips to residual nerve clusters. Magnetic cuff locks to most mid-grade chrome housings. Half-finger variant allows direct digital contact for biometric access points.
what_it_says: You've got chrome and you're not hiding it — you're making it work better than the factory default.
worn_by: prosthetic limb wearers seeking tactile feedback
story_hooks: A glove pulled from a drainage canal still has a partial handprint burned into its haptic film — and the chrome it was paired with is missing from its registered owner.
Nullframe quietly recalled batch 7-C after users reported phantom pain feedback loops; the recall was never publicized and thousands of affected pairs are still in circulation.
A Tier 3 accountant wearing one of these keeps receiving haptic signals that don't correspond to anything their chrome is touching — someone is spoofing the relay frequency.
